vista.build: Rebuilt the vista's atmosphere and dressing: the sky now has a real gradient (luminous horizon band to deep navy zenith) with an HDR moon as the brightest element plus soft halo, thin low clouds and sparse stars; fog colour follows the sky gradient so far ridges dissolve instead of reading paler than the sky; a new one-draw-call Shafts module lays soft moonlight beams across the misty valley and Postfx adds a screen-space moon halo; a shadowless cool fill light makes camera-facing facets step apart. The ground went from a carpet of identical ochre tufts to sparse 3-tint clumps over warm faceted turf with boulders at both frame edges, a new slab `cliff` prop forms sheer rock bands on the spur (~100 m) and the far cliff band (~300 m) with explicit ruin fragments at each depth. Triangles cut from 1.13 M to ~594 k (incl. shadow + post) at 320 draw calls, zero console errors; CHANGELOG updated (render + world lines, plus notes on the ring veil and HMR-interrupted captures).

character.gap: B's character is lit flat and front-on even though the moon sits directly behind it at top-centre: the blue tunic and hood are a single uniform value with no gradient, no rim/edge light on the shoulders or hood, and no occlusion where cloak, belt and pouches meet the body. Combined with constant-diameter tube limbs ending in a yellow sphere hand and capsule boots, the hero reads as unshaded primitives pasted over the backdrop rather than a sculpted figure sitting in that fog.
character.fix: Key the character shader to the scene light: add a cool white-blue rim/backlight aligned to the moon direction (fresnel-driven, roughly 1.5x key intensity) so hood, shoulders and cloak edge catch a bright outline against the fog, drop the camera-facing fill by about 30 percent so the back of the torso falls into a soft gradient, and bake a light AO gradient at hood/cloak/belt junctions; while in the model, taper forearm-to-wrist and calf-to-ankle and replace the sphere hand with a wedge mitt.
character.notes: A's hero is genuinely sculpted (layered collar, belt, satchel, wrapped boots, real taper through the limbs) and shares the cave's soft bounced light and a true contact shadow on the rock, so it reads as one coherent art direction rather than a figure composited onto a scene.
character.build: Re-shaded the hero in src/entity/Humanoid.js: RigBuilder.build gained opt-in crease-aware (60°) area-weighted smooth normals and a point-based per-vertex AO bake (two-sided disc form factors on a grid, baked in a spread pose via a new posed() skinning pass so bind-pose limbs stop occluding each other, plus ground darkening and a painted mottle), the body material now shades smooth/matte with a moon-side fresnel rim instead of a uniform outline, limbs re-lofted with designed taper (deltoid 2.6x wrist, hip 2x ankle), costume pulled toward the muted stone/leather palette, hood given a drooping peak and wider drape. The run clip's sword arm now carries the forearm level with the blade pitched +16° in world space (tip 1.18 m up, 1.3 m ahead, never below 0.66 m through the cycle) so it no longer drives into the ground, and the cloak sway moved into a GLSL function whose finite differences give smooth cloth normals (darker, less level, calmer folds). Other rigs are untouched (opt-in), zero console errors, 10k-vertex rig bakes in ~50 ms at build.

combat.gap: No impact is happening in A: the player's polearm is carried in a run pose with no swing arc or trail, neither enemy is reacting to a hit, and there is no hit flash, spark, or foot dust — and the flat overcast lighting lets the dark hooded enemy melt into the grass and trees behind it. It reads as "jogging toward a skirmish," not a weighty hit landing.
combat.fix: Re-stage on the contact frame: freeze the polearm at the end of a horizontal swing with a short, hard-edged ribbon trail; put the hooded enemy in a recoil pose (torso thrown back, rear foot sliding) with a tight radial spark burst at the blade contact point and dust puffs under both figures' feet; add a warm key/rim light from camera-left so the dark enemy separates from the busy midground.
combat.notes: B stages the exact beat — a luminous weapon trail terminating in a spark burst on a plate-armoured, crested knight mid-recoil, a second enemy winding up by the fire, dust at the feet — with the campfire as a warm key against a cool night giving clean figure separation; its weakness is environment dressing (flat-shaded box buildings and prism tents), not the combat read.
combat.build: Re-kitted the struck Soldier in src/entity/enemies/EnemyRig.js for value separation (crested wide-brim kettle helm over a charcoal aventail, one big three-lame pauldron on the shield shoulder, charcoal tabard with bone trim and emblem, greaves, bone-cross shield, gold knight crest) and added ENEMY_CLIPS with a mirror-capable held hit-stop `recoil` (torso bent back and rolled away, near arm flung, far arm thrown up, rear leg skidding) that gameplay now uses for heavy blows (src/entity/Enemy.js). Combat FX were reworked: the weapon trail is a premultiplied MAX-blended crescent (no more additive blob), impact() drives a new warm HIT_RIM uniform in the enemy shader so the spark burst wraps the struck body's edges, skidDust() drags a smear from a sliding foot, and dust is paler so it reads on the dirt. The combat pose (src/combat/Pose.js) was mirrored: camera over the hero's left shoulder, a light2 cut with a chest roll baked through the trail samples for a high-to-low diagonal, the soldier planted big right-of-centre on the blade in the recoil with the impact light/rim anchored on the contact, the fire centred as a backlight with the knight's heated wind-up silhouetted beside it and the wolf crouched left; tools/screenshot.mjs keeps dying on parallel Vite reloads, so the final capture came from a retrying scratch script (the official tool also reported zero console errors).

ring.gap: The night ring — the subject of the piece — is demoted to a knee-high band of blue flame in the mid-background, mostly occluded by six overlapping combatants and a cropped dark foreground figure eating the left third of the frame; there is no towering wall, no contact rim on the terrain, no cold-tinted interior, and no scale relationship between a player and the front, so the frame reads as a generic melee shot rather than 'the night closing in'.
ring.fix: Recompose for the subject: pull the camera back and low behind a single player, remove the foreground occluder and extra combatants, and extend the blue flame band vertically into a screen-height translucent curtain with downward rain streaks and a bright contact rim along the grass line, so the wall owns the upper two-thirds of the frame and the player sits small against it.
ring.notes: A actually delivers the piece: a screen-height streaking curtain with flame-like tongues at the terrain contact, cold-tinted ground beyond it, warm embers against the blue, and a tiny player for scale — though B wins decisively on raw material and lighting fidelity, which is why this is a lean rather than a sure.
ring.build: Rebuilt the night ring as a weather front with real vertical volume: the wall shells are now a deep-navy fresnel veil (dense where it curves away, thin facing the camera) that dissolves over the bottom metres so the fire and ground pool own the terrain contact, carrying sparse tall falling-light curtains, drifting nebula cells, and crisp blue fire tongues 4–12 m tall with thin pale cores and a broken-up base; the rain is a 1100-streak curtain confined to a band about the wall so the player stands in dry air, the world hook adds a capped saturated-blue fire band, a cold night fog beyond the wall and a fresnel fire rim on trunks/rocks/the player, and motes cluster at the fire. The pose moved off the flattened arena to the grassy overlook crest (player left of centre, wall 12 m ahead downslope, blue-lit dead trees beyond, hero tree framing right, HUD countdown + proximity warning). Official capture has zero console errors, smoke test 27/27.

hud.build: Re-matched the HUD to the Nightreign gameplay frames: bar tracks are a dark well inside a light hairline with muted brick/teal/moss fills and cream tips, lag trails on every bar (cream HP, yellow stamina, pale-blue FP), the flask row under the bars and the raised item slot both show the golden flask with its count (Player gained a flasks/maxFlasks stub refilled at grace/respawn), a fire-pot sub-slot, a hairline-framed rune counter with a twelve-spoke wheel, sword-with-rays/crescent art glyphs, a 7 px boss bar on a warm track, and a slightly larger reticle; fixed the ult square stacking over the flask icon (absolute SLOT constant). The hud pose now uses a near-level camera (pitch -0.02, dist 6.4) so the whole Sentinel and its raised halberd sit under the moon over the bosses builder's new joined flagstones, with the player at 55% HP, lock-on reticle on the boss chest, and the boss mid wind-up. Final capture has zero console errors; a reload-tolerant live probe confirmed the un-posed HUD path (trail hold/drain, flask counts, layout) runs clean.

architecture.gap: A has no ambient occlusion or contact shadowing anywhere: every facet is one flat value (lit or unlit) and the buttresses, broken-wall fragments and gravestones meet a single flat olive ground plane with zero darkening at the base, so the masses float and read as extruded boxes dropped on a plane rather than masonry rooted in a hill — exactly the "boxes" the brief warns against.
architecture.fix: Do a grounding pass: enable SSAO (or bake AO into vertex colours) and add a vertex-colour "foundation band" that darkens the bottom ~1 m of every wall, buttress and gravestone mesh, then lay a lighter trodden-dirt decal/ground band from the gate to the church door so the ground has at least two values and the church visibly sits in the terrain.
architecture.notes: B wins on lighting doing the work — volumetric god rays, warm bounce in recesses, a value ramp from dark foreground floor to bright far arch, and recesses that read as real depth — giving scale and material credibility that A's flat per-facet shading never reaches; note B is off-brief (intact palace corridor, no ruin, no fog, no hill), but its craft lead is decisive.
architecture.build: Rebuilt the church as a real ruin and re-composed all three architecture poses. Structures.js: Kit gained per-quad facet jitter, a stronger base/damp gradient, low-frequency weathering, inside-corner AO from registered occluder boxes, halo-free fires (warm bake without the hovering glow disc), a beam() primitive and a wrap-lit structure material so moon-shadow faces are mid blue-grey instead of black; the church now has ruinWall column walls with 3-7 stepped jagged heights per wall (breach on the camera side, far wall's rear half at ~40%), no roof slab but nine A-frame rafter pairs (two snapped, two fallen into the nave, sagging ridge, slates clinging to the rear bays), 1.3x1.5 m stepped buttresses on every bay, crow-stepped west gable with a sky-through great window over a two-order porch, a three-stage tower with clasping buttresses, blind arcading, belfry lancets, corbel table, broken parapet and collapsed-spire stump, tumbled ashlar at the wall feet and an east burial plot on the measured slope; POI.js gained ruinWall/blindArcade/corbelTable; the fort got halo-free causeway/curtain torches and the ruin a jagged-column gable with buttresses. New world/Pose.js compositions (church from the front-right with the grace behind the camera, fort from the east flank below the plateau, ruin from the high ground against the misty basin) are wired via a minimal Debug.js delegation; official capture run reports zero console errors.

bosses.gap: The boss in B is an illegible lump: mount body, neck, head and rider torso are all the same near-black boxy mass with no value separation, so the horse and knight merge into one blob and the only thing that reads is the halberd sticking out of it. The silhouette is supposed to sell the threat, and here it sells a stack of crates with a flat red rectangle hung off the side; the player's chibi figure in front reads more clearly than the boss does.
bosses.fix: Rebuild the mount/rider as two opposed shapes with a hard value split: make the horse a long, low, near-black horizontal mass with a clearly extended neck and head (ears, muzzle) projecting forward past the rider and four separated legs in a wide stance; make the rider a pale steel-grey vertical form with a tall crested helm sitting on top of it; then add a cool moon rim-light along the top-right edge of both so the outline is carved against the sky. One dark horizontal + one light vertical gives an instantly readable "mounted knight" silhouette at any distance.
bosses.notes: A has fully resolved materials and a single unified lighting scheme (warm fire key against cool blue-grey sky) that lights every character, the shattered stone slabs and the airborne debris identically, so the whole frame reads as one coherent world rather than assets dropped onto a plane.
bosses.build: Replaced the boss arena's scattered box slabs and blown-out gold disc with a continuous paved-floor decal (new Paving.js: running-bond flagstones with grout, joint AO, per-slab value/tilt variation, missing slabs, ragged rim; draws first with no depth write so the player's contact blobs, the boss blob and the thin telegraph ring sit on it, and it receives the player's long moon shadow) and redrew the telegraph as a thin soft rim (~2.5% of radius) whose fill edge merges into the rim. Gave the Gate Sentinel real material separation: a new armour material set (BossRig.armourMats) with a specular flat-facet plate slot plus per-material cool-rim/sky-fill/warm-torch-rim uniforms pointed at the nearest brazier each frame, and a two-tone palette (blued steel + brass rider; black hide, crimson caparison, leather mount); diagnosed that this pipeline's emissive reads ~10x hot, so the body telegraph glow and ember light were cut to accents. Arena mid-ground now frames the boss (ruined gate piers + broken lintel left, gibbet silhouette right), brazier flames are registered in limveld.fires so the world's torch point light and embers follow the arena, and the pose parks that light before capture.
